newsitem.title: UK: Euro conversion costs for firms seen low - study.
newsitem.headline: Euro conversion costs for firms seen low - study.

text.p: The costs for securities firms of converting operations to the new euro currency will be only a fraction of total operating costs and much lower than previously estimated, a study by the International Securities Market Association (ISMA) said on Thursday.
"Euro conversion costs amounted to an average of 0.00058 percent of total operating costs of financial institutions," a study commissioned by ISMA said.
"The maximum cost reported by firms active in the securities market is approximately eight million Ecu, with the lowest being 110,000 Ecu," the study said.
"These figures are substantially lower than many previously stated cost estimates," the study said.
"Previous figures have referred to entire financial markets and embraced both retail and wholesale segments of the financial industry and have not been limited to the securities market."
ISMA said the costs reported in its survey purely reflected conversion costs to the euro and not the ongoing upgrading of information technology systems, which were not euro-driven.
The report, called "The cost and time-scale for the switch-over to the euro for the international securities market" was commissioned by ISMA and 900 securities firms participated.
"The majority of securities firms feel confident practical conversion can occur fairly smoothly with relatively short notice and little preparation time," ISMA said.
